---
title: "Recovery Checkpoint 3: Ready for Modeling"
description: "A short optional recovery route before the modeling phase."
---

This checkpoint consolidates reusable functions, vectorization, iteration, and
batch evidence before modeling begins. It is not an extra assignment unless
the instructor says otherwise.

## Minimum Foundation

You should be able to:

- turn repeated code into a function with a clear input-output contract;
- test normal, boundary, and failure cases;
- separate import, cleaning, analysis, and reporting stages;
- choose vectorized operations or iteration without hiding errors;
- retain a status record for every requested file, group, or model;
- produce named outputs whose rows stay aligned with their inputs;
- rerun the workflow from a clean session.

## A 45-60 Minute Recovery Route

1. Rerun the [Week 12 repeated workflow](../code/r/week12-repeated-workflow.R).
2. Complete core Exercises 1, 2, and 4 from [Week 11](week-11-exercises.qmd)
   and Exercises 1, 2, and 4 from [Week 12](week-12-exercises.qmd).
3. Choose one repeated task and write its contract: accepted input, returned
   output, one boundary case, and one informative failure.
4. Confirm that every requested input produces either a result row or an
   explicit failure-status row.

## Ready To Continue?

You are ready when another person can run your saved workflow, trace one output
back to its input, and see failures without reconstructing your working memory.
